new_candidates_identified.problem_name: CSF-venous fistula in spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH)
new_candidates_identified.problem_description: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) is caused by CSF leaks, often via CSF-venous fistulas (abnormal connections between CSF space and venous system). Current treatment is epidural blood patch (EBP), which is often temporary — 'blood patch is thought to treat CSF venous fistulas based on transient compression alone thereby decreasing the durability' (White 2024). Surgical treatment and glue embolization are invasive alternatives.

problem_exists_evidence.evidence: White 2024 (cited 3), Konovalov 2022 (cited 34), Callen 2024 (cited 38). CSF-venous fistulas are a recognized cause of SIH. EBP is first-line but durability is limited.
problem_exists_evidence.incidence: SIH prevalence ~1/50,000. CSF-venous fistulas are a subset.
problem_exists_evidence.clinical_severity: HIGH — severe orthostatic headaches, disability, risk of subdural hematoma

new_candidates_identified.buyer_impact: This is a DIFFERENT problem from hydrocephalus. eShunt drains CSF FROM SAS TO venous. A CSF-venous fistula is an UNWANTED connection between CSF and venous. The eShunt platform's knowledge of the CSF-venous interface could be applied to SEAL fistulas, not create them. But this is a fundamentally different intervention — sealing vs draining.
new_candidates_identified.existing_solutions_gap: EBP is temporary. Surgery is invasive. Glue embolization is technically challenging. No permanent, minimally-invasive solution exists.
new_candidates_identified.causal_mechanism_direction: An endovascular approach to SEAL CSF-venous fistulas from the venous side — using the eShunt's venous-sinus access to deliver a permanent seal (mechanical, biological, or thermal) to the fistula. This is a FUNDAMENTALLY DIFFERENT causal mechanism from EBP (compression) or surgery (direct repair).
new_candidates_identified.ce_cemetery_check: NO cemetery overlap. This is a new problem class.
new_candidates_identified.physical_plausibility: MEDIUM — sealing a fistula from the venous side is mechanically feasible (similar to vascular embolization). The challenge is identifying and accessing the fistula site.

new_candidates_identified.problem_description: Some hydrocephalus cases are caused by CSF over-production by the choroid plexus, rather than impaired drainage. Current treatments (VP shunt, ETV) address drainage but NOT the underlying over-production. Choroid plexus coagulation exists but is invasive and non-selective. Pharmacological treatments (acetazolamide) 'provide only symptomatic relief and do not address the underlying' cause (Anwar 2024, Sluijters 2026).

problem_exists_evidence.evidence: Anwar 2024 (cited 27): 'The most effective current pharmacological treatments provide only symptomatic relief and do not address' the underlying cause. Koleva 2023 (cited 98): choroid plexus coagulation is an option but invasive. Sluijters 2026: current treatment 'does not address the underlying' cause.
problem_exists_evidence.incidence: CSF over-production is a subset of hydrocephalus (exact fraction unclear, but clinically recognized)

new_candidates_identified.buyer_impact: If eShunt can be adapted to MODULATE CSF production (not just drainage), it addresses the ROOT CAUSE of over-production hydrocephalus. This is a different value proposition from drainage-only shunts.
new_candidates_identified.existing_solutions_gap: Acetazolamide is symptomatic, not curative. Choroid plexus coagulation is invasive and non-selective (destroys tissue). No existing solution provides CONTROLLED, REVERSIBLE modulation of CSF production.
new_candidates_identified.causal_mechanism_direction: An eShunt-integrated approach to modulate choroid plexus activity — e.g., localized drug delivery to the choroid plexus, or electrical neuromodulation of choroid plexus function. This is a FUNDAMENTALLY DIFFERENT causal mechanism from drainage-based shunts.
new_candidates_identified.ce_cemetery_check: NO direct cemetery overlap. But overlaps with Slot 3 (CV-T03 controlled therapeutic delivery) if the mechanism is drug delivery. Must distinguish: Slot 3 = drug delivery FOR THERAPEUTIC RETENTION; S5-C09 = modulation of CSF PRODUCTION.
new_candidates_identified.physical_plausibility: MEDIUM — the choroid plexus is anatomically accessible via the ventricular system. But an eShunt is deployed in the venous sinus, not the ventricle. Reaching the choroid plexus from the venous sinus would require a different access path or a remotely-acting mechanism (e.g., drug delivered via CSF that reaches choroid plexus).
